_comment: credential-inventory.v1.json — data for ops/credential-health.py (the daily credential-health lane wired into tools/health-check.py). One entry per credential CARR needs to run unattended. Adding a credential later is a config edit here, not a code change. NEVER put a secret VALUE in this file — same rule secrets-inventory.md states for itself. Built 2026-09-24 off Joe's survey: CARR is moving off interactive logins to long-lived scoped tokens, and this lane is what tells him before one lapses. Every row carries exactly one of `self_mintable_from` (the root grant in ops/config/credential-root-grants.v1.json the nightly 'credential mint' step mints and rotates it from once that grant is placed) or `holder_only` (why no provider API can mint it, so a human keeps holding it); lib/credential_mint.load_plan() refuses the two files when they disagree.
_probe_types: shell_exit_status (run `command`, exit code only, stdout/stderr discarded) | cloudflare_auth (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN env if set -> Cloudflare token-verify endpoint, HTTP status + expires_on field only; else falls back to shell_exit_status's `command` — retained for a machine that has not migrated off `wrangler login` yet) | cloudflare_token_file (reads token_key out of the dotenv-shaped file at `path`, mode-600-checked, never the wrangler fallback -> Cloudflare token-verify endpoint, HTTP status + result.status + result.expires_on only) | claude_cli_token_age (reads token_key out of the dotenv-shaped file at `path`, checks length/prefix shape, runs `claude -p "Reply with exactly: PONG" --max-turns 1` from a throwaway cwd with ONLY that one env var set and scans only for the word PONG, and ages the token from a first-seen mint date this lane records itself in out/credential-health-mint-state.json — never the token value) | neon_api (reads token_key out of the dotenv-shaped file at `path` if configured and present, else NEON_API_KEY env -> GET /projects?org_id=<the CARR org> on Neon's API — the question an organization API key can answer, and the one tools/rotate-credential.py verifies a rotated key with — HTTP status only; 401/403 is failed, any other non-2xx is unknown with the status in the detail) | worker_bearer_health (reads token_key out of the dotenv-shaped file at `path` if configured and present, else the token_env env var -> POST tools/list against the deployed Worker's /mcp; ok requires BOTH HTTP 200 and a JSON-RPC `result` key in the body, never anything inside it) | file_presence_age (local file's existence + mtime age, never its contents) | config_only (no live probe; status comes entirely from the `expiry` block below, which Joe edits by hand)

credentials.name: cloudflare-deploy-token
credentials.replacement_plan: ROTATED BY THE SYSTEM once the Cloudflare root grant is placed (one time: `.venv/bin/python tools/store-token.py CLOUDFLARE_TOKEN_ROOT`): the nightly 'credential mint' step (ops/credential-mint.py) mints a fresh child every 90 days, verifies it with a read-only call made by the new child, stores it as CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN in ~/.config/carr/tokens.env, and revokes the previous one. Children are user-owned tokens scoped to the CARR account with Workers Scripts:Edit + Account Settings:Read, so this probe's /user/tokens/verify keeps working unchanged. Until the root grant is placed, a failing probe is fixed by hand: mint the same scoped token in the dashboard and run `.venv/bin/python tools/store-token.py CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`. If the finding is insecure_file_permissions rather than the token itself, `chmod 600 ~/.config/carr/tokens.env` is the whole fix — the token does not need to be rotated for that alone.

credentials.name: claude-cli-oauth-token-studio
credentials.display_name: Claude Code CLI long-lived login (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, Studio)
credentials.replacement_plan: Already the long-lived scoped replacement for the interactive Claude Code CLI login, minted by `claude setup-token` (2026-09-24, ~1 year validity). If this probe fails or reports expiring_soon, run `claude setup-token` again, paste the new value into ~/.config/carr/tokens.env as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=<value>, and confirm the file stays mode 600. A rotated token resets this lane's own age tracking on its next run (it re-records today as the mint date the first time it sees the new value's fingerprint).
credentials.holder_only: Anthropic offers no API that mints a Claude Code OAuth token: `claude setup-token` is a browser sign-in only the account holder completes.
credentials.doc_pointer: CLAUDE.md — Dell migration trigger section (Claude-only launch machine)

credentials.name: neon-api-key
credentials.replacement_plan: ROTATED BY THE SYSTEM once the Neon root grant is placed (one time: `.venv/bin/python tools/store-token.py NEON_ORG_ROOT_KEY`): the nightly 'credential mint' step (ops/credential-mint.py) mints a fresh child every 90 days, verifies it with a read-only call made by the new child, stores it as NEON_API_KEY in ~/.config/carr/db.env, and revokes the previous one. Children are organization API keys of org org-dry-dew-75906281, so this probe asks the question an org key answers (GET /projects?org_id=...). The personal key placed by hand before the root grant existed is left in place on the first system rotation (its id is unknown to the lane); delete it in the Neon console once. Until the root grant is placed, rotate by hand with tools/rotate-credential.py --neon-api-key.

credentials.name: carr-mcp-probe-token
credentials.replacement_plan: Server-issued bearer, already long-lived and scoped to the locked 'probe' profile (mcp-server/src/mcp.js). If it fails, Joe re-mints it with `wrangler secret put PROBE_TOKENS` per the runbook in mcp-server/smoke-reads.sh's header and re-pastes the matching value into mcp-tokens.env; no agent ever holds it.
credentials.holder_only: CARR's own Worker issues it from the PROBE_TOKENS Worker secret; there is no provider mint API, and minting it means a Worker secret write plus redeploy, which the mint lane does not do.

credentials.name: carr-mcp-local-token
credentials.replacement_plan: Server-issued bearer, already long-lived, one per machine (joe-local / dell-local). If it fails, Joe re-mints via `wrangler secret put LOCAL_TOKENS` per pipelines/provision-local-client.sql and re-pastes the matching value on the affected machine; no agent ever holds it.
credentials.holder_only: CARR's own Worker issues it from the LOCAL_TOKENS Worker secret, one per machine; there is no provider mint API, and minting it means a Worker secret write plus redeploy, which the mint lane does not do.

credentials.name: gh-cli-auth
credentials.replacement_plan: ALREADY SELF-MINTING for unattended use: every background gh call derives a fresh GitHub App installation token from the CARR GitHub App key (lib/github_app_token.gh_env), so nothing unattended depends on this interactive `gh auth` login; it remains only for Joe's own hand use. The app key is the root grant (one time: `bin/github-app-key-intake.sh`); the nightly 'credential mint' step files a loop if it is missing. A failing probe here means only the interactive login lapsed: `gh auth login` when Joe next needs gh by hand.

expiry._note: Joe sets configured_rotation_date (YYYY-MM-DD) here once the fine-grained PAT exists and carries an expiry; null means no configured window and the probe result stands on its own.

credentials.name: codex-cli-auth-studio
credentials.replacement_plan: ROTATED BY THE SYSTEM once the OpenAI root grant is placed (one time: `.venv/bin/python tools/store-token.py OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY`): the nightly 'credential mint' step (ops/credential-mint.py) mints a fresh child every 90 days, verifies it with a read-only call made by the new child, stores it as OPENAI_API_KEY in ~/.config/carr/tokens.env, installs it into Codex with `codex login --with-api-key` (value on stdin), and revokes the previous one. Each child is a service account of the OpenAI project carr-system. This moves Codex on the Studio from ChatGPT-subscription auth to metered API-key auth. A row is minted only by the lane running ON the machine it names. The complete absence of ~/.codex is an expected supported state on a Claude-only launch machine (CLAUDE.md, Dell migration trigger) — this row reports `unknown` there, never `failed`.

credentials.name: codex-cli-auth-macbook
credentials.replacement_plan: ROTATED BY THE SYSTEM once the OpenAI root grant is placed (one time: `.venv/bin/python tools/store-token.py OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY`): the nightly 'credential mint' step (ops/credential-mint.py) mints a fresh child every 90 days, verifies it with a read-only call made by the new child, stores it as OPENAI_API_KEY in ~/.config/carr/tokens.env, installs it into Codex with `codex login --with-api-key` (value on stdin), and revokes the previous one. Each child is a service account of the OpenAI project carr-system. This moves Codex on the MacBook from ChatGPT-subscription auth to metered API-key auth. A row is minted only by the lane running ON the machine it names — the nightly chain runs on the primary (Studio), so this MacBook row rotates only when ops/credential-mint.py runs on the MacBook. The complete absence of ~/.codex is an expected supported state on a Claude-only launch machine (CLAUDE.md, Dell migration trigger) — this row reports `unknown` there, never `failed`.

credentials.name: google-oauth-worker-client
credentials.location: Worker secret (wrangler); OAuth client in Google Cloud project carr-record-layer
credentials.replacement_plan: No local probe is possible — Joe holds this credential and no agent ever has (secrets-inventory.md). If the Google Cloud consent screen is still in 'testing' publishing status, Google expires the refresh token after 7 days; the fix is Joe publishing the consent screen (removes the 7-day cap) or re-consenting within the window. Set `expiry.google_testing_mode` true and `expiry.consent_screen_last_verified` to today whenever Joe re-verifies, so this row can compute the live window.
credentials.holder_only: Google offers no API to mint or publish a consumer OAuth client's secret or consent screen; both are Google Cloud console acts by the project owner.

expiry._note: Joe sets google_testing_mode (true/false) and consent_screen_last_verified (YYYY-MM-DD, the date he last confirmed the consent screen state) by hand. Both null means 'not yet configured' and the row reports unknown rather than guessing.

credentials.name: grok-cli-auth
credentials.location: Grok CLI's own credential store (`grok login`; ~/.grok)
credentials.replacement_plan: Grok runs on the SuperGrok grok.com login (bin/council-lib.sh billing note), not a metered API key. If this probe fails, Joe runs `grok login --oauth` (or `--device-auth` on a headless session). No root grant can replace it: see holder_only.
credentials.holder_only: The Grok CLI signs in only through grok.com OAuth (`grok login` offers --oauth and --device-auth, no API-key mode), so no xAI management key can mint or install its login.
